vulnerabilities: Overwhelming trade dependence on the United States (the large majority of Canadian exports go to the US), creating acute exposure to US tariff or trade-policy shifts
Below-NATO-target defence spending historically, with limited standing conventional force size relative to landmass
Vast, sparsely monitored Arctic coastline creates sovereignty and surveillance gaps as melting ice opens new shipping routes contested by Russia and, increasingly, China
Defence procurement historically slow and cost-overrun-prone, delaying fleet and equipment modernisation
strengths: NORAD binational air-defence integration with the US provides continental early-warning and air-defence coverage
Major net exporter of energy (oil sands), critical minerals, and agricultural commodities
G7 member with deep Five Eyes intelligence integration and NATO membership
Sole non-Russian claimant with a credible (if still developing) Arctic sovereignty presence via the Northwest Passage
